title: High-Resolution Fluorescence Microscopy-Based 3D Encoding Using Polarity-Sensitive Dyes for Rapid Screening of Microplastics in Complex Environmental Samples.
mesh: Microscopy, Fluorescence; Microplastics; Fluorescent Dyes; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Imaging, Three-Dimensional
abstract: Microplastics (MPs), as emerging pollutants of global concern, urgently require rapid monitoring techniques for effective ecological risk management. Fluorescence microscopy is widely utilized for capturing the morphology of MPs but remains limited in polymer-type discrimination and differentiation from environmental matrices. Herein, we present a novel fluorescence microscopy-based three-dimensional (3D) encoding strategy employing three polarity-sensitive dyes (DNAS, DCM, and MONS) for rapid screening of MPs in complex environmental matrices. Owing to differences in the surface polarity of MPs, the adsorbed polarity-sensitive dyes undergo intramolecular charge transfer (ICT). The polarity-dependent stabilization of the excited charge-transfer state alters the emission energy, resulting in distinct fluorescence colors on different MPs. The three dyes also exhibited varied ICT responses due to hydrogen-bonding and dipole-dipole interactions between the surface groups of MPs and the dyes, facilitating encoding-based discrimination. Stained images were captured with a self-constructed portable fluorescence microscope. The images were converted from RGB values into CIE L*a*b* coordinates to construct a 3D encoding library, where triangular or linear pattern encoding greatly enhanced the spatial separation of MPs and sample matrices. This method enabled rapid identification of 12 common MP types and clear differentiation from ten natural nonplastic matrices. The CIE L*a*b* coordinates exhibited good repeatability, with RSD values of 0.69-4.99% (n = 10). Both "known-as-unknown" spiked sample validation and the analysis of real environmental samples demonstrate that the proposed workflow can rapidly identify polymer types in complex samples, with the results agreeing well with those obtained by FTIR. This low-cost, portable, and spectrometer-free strategy offers a practical tool for rapid screening of MPs in complex environmental samples.

title: "Imaging Triplets on Two Wheels": 61Cu-, 64Cu-, and 68Ga-labeled Bicyclic Peptides Targeting Nectin-4 Enable High-Contrast PET Imaging of Urothelial Carcinoma and Triple-Negative Breast Cancer.
mesh: Humans; Animals; Nectins; Copper Radioisotopes; Female; Triple Negative Breast Neoplasms; Positron-Emission Tomography; Mice; Cell Line, Tumor; Urologic Neoplasms; Peptides, Cyclic; Radiopharmaceuticals; Gallium Radioisotopes
abstract: Nectin-4 is a validated target for theranostic approaches toward urothelial carcinoma, and radiolabeled ligands for PET and SPECT imaging are gaining increasing interest for noninvasive quantification of Nectin-4 prior to a targeted therapy. The goal of this study was to develop bicyclic peptides that allow radiolabeling with three different radionuclides (61Cu, 64Cu, and 68Ga) and to evaluate their suitability for high-contrast PET imaging in urothelial carcinoma (UC) and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). For this purpose, NECT-330, NECT-334, and NECT-346 were designed based on our previously developed ligand NECT-224 but harbor additional linker units between the bicyclic scaffold and the radiometal chelator. Binding kinetics to recombinant Nectin-4 and related isoforms were assessed by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) interaction analysis. Nectin-4-specific cell binding of the radiolabeled probes was determined using UC and TNBC cell lines, and PET/CT imaging was performed in respective tumor xenograft models. All novel ligands showed potent and selective binding to Nectin-4, with improved koff values compared to NECT-224. In small-animal PET/CT imaging studies, the most favorable properties were observed for [64Cu]Cu-NECT-334 (tumor-to-muscle of 20.8 and tumor-to-heart of 11.2) and [64Cu]Cu-NECT-346 (tumor-to-muscle of 15.5 and tumor-to-heart of 8.7) 1-2 h postinjection using a HT-1376 tumor model. Although the novel radioligands provided superior imaging properties to the previously developed radioligand [64Cu]Cu-NECT-224, a first-in-human application of the latter radioligand was initiated to assess the general suitability of PET/CT imaging in humans with a 64Cu-labeled bicyclic peptide directed to Nectin-4. Prospectively, the improved tumor-to-background contrasts achieved with the novel radioligands might further improve diagnostic accuracy and facilitate effective theranostic options in Nectin-4-expressing malignancies.

title: Hydrolytic-Peroxidatic Cascade on Bifunctional Nanozymes for Specific Fluorescent Profiling of Aromatic Polyester Microplastics.
mesh: Microplastics; Polyesters; Hydrolysis; Fluorescence; Nanostructures; Phthalic Acids
abstract: Aromatic polyester microplastics are derived from a special type of engineering plastic. Therefore, effective management requires reliable qualitative discrimination and accurate quantitative detection, rather than simply measuring total microplastic concentrations. To address this challenge, we developed a cascading fluorescence sensing platform based on the sequential dual-enzyme mimicry of magnesium-iron layered double oxide (MgFe LDO) nanozymes. MgFe LDO first hydrolyzes aromatic polyesters into terephthalic acid (TPA), which is subsequently hydroxylated via its peroxidase-mimicking activity to generate the fluorescent product 2-hydroxyterephthalic acid. Differences in hydrolysis rate and TPA concentration arising from the structural variation among distinct aromatic polyesters are translated into quantifiable fluorescence signals, enabling the precise detection and specific discrimination of multiple polymers. The bifunctional nanozymes combining hydrolase-like and peroxidase-like activities exhibit reliable performance and adaptability in spiked real-world samples, including rainwater, river water, tap water, and seawater. This work provides a basis for constructing integrated laboratory-based screening platforms for aromatic polyester microplastics using rationally engineered nanozymes.

title: Prior-Attention-Mechanism-Based Spectral Identifier for Revealing Hazardous Chemical Additives in Commercial PVC.
mesh: Polyvinyl Chloride; Hazardous Substances; Spectrum Analysis, Raman
abstract: Additive components largely determine the environmental and health risks of commercial plastics, but rapid, nondestructive identification of multiple additives in polymer matrices remains challenging. To overcome this challenge, we developed a prior-knowledge-guided triple-scale convolutional neural network (SpecNet) that identified 14 additive classes and two polyvinyl chloride (PVC) types from microconfocal Raman spectra. SpecNet integrated spectral chunking, cross-attention with characteristic peak embedding, and a combined BCE and L1 loss for joint classification and semiquantitative ranking of additive abundances. Trained on 2,200 spectra, the model achieved a 95.03% F1-score on an independent environmental test set (1,000 spectra). Platt scaling reduced the Brier score to 0.03, and Monte Carlo dropout uncertainty was <0.05 when SNR > 10. The model-assisted detection threshold for tris(1-chloro-2-propyl) phosphate (TCPP) reached 2.5 wt %, approximately 2-fold lower than the conventional visual detection limit of Raman spectroscopy (∼5 wt %) by leveraging learned multipeak patterns and prior-knowledge attention to extract weak signals below visual detectability. In zero-shot tests on non-PVC polymers, SpecNet correctly identified additives in 82.8% of cases. For additives in microplastic samples after accelerated photoaging (90 days, ∼15 years natural exposure), it maintained 92.48% identification accuracy by dynamically lowering the detection threshold from 0.5 to 0.005. SpecNet offers an interpretable, field-deployable tool for screening hazardous plastic additives in environmental monitoring, recycling, and risk assessment.

title: Release and Transformation of Polymer-Associated Chemicals from Aged Polypropylene and Polyurethane Microplastics in Freshwater Laboratory and Mesocosm Studies.
mesh: Polyurethanes; Microplastics; Polypropylenes; Fresh Water; Water Pollutants, Chemical; Polymers
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) release polymer-associated chemicals (PACs) into aquatic environments, yet their environmental release, transformation, and persistence remain poorly understood. We applied nontargeted liquid chromatography high-resolution mass spectrometry to characterize PACs released from polypropylene (PP) and polyurethane (PU) MPs in complementary 12-month freshwater wetland mesocosm and 3-month laboratory photolysis and leaching experiments. More leachable compounds were detected from PP (128) than PU (34), reflecting differences in polymer formulations and physicochemical properties. Laboratory studies identified readily mobilized and transformable PACs, including the PP additive bis(2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-4-piperidyl)sebacate (BTMS) and the PU monomer 4-(4-formamidobenzyl)phenyl formamide. Laboratory experiments using higher MP concentrations (10,000 mg L-1) prioritized target PACs for monitoring in lower-concentration mesocosms (50 mg L-1), where ricinine was quantified in PU treatments and BTMS and 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-4-piperidinol (TMPO) were quantified in PP treatments. PAC concentrations increased over time under simplified laboratory conditions but declined in environmentally complex mesocosms, suggesting environmental attenuation through processes such as sorption, sedimentation, and microbial degradation that require further confirmation in future studies. UV exposure minimally affected BTMS hydrolysis but promoted ricinine photodegradation and the formation of additional PU-derived transformation products. These findings identified environmentally relevant PACs and demonstrated the value of integrating simplified laboratory studies with environmentally realistic mesocosms to improve PAC identification and evaluate environmental fate.

title: Surface Biogeochemical Regimes Shape Microplastic Abundance in the Eastern Indian Ocean.
mesh: Water Pollutants, Chemical; Microplastics; Indian Ocean
abstract: Open-ocean microplastic (MP) abundance is commonly reported as a contamination metric, but surface concentrations may reflect environmental redistribution, dilution, and retention in addition to source exposure. Here, we investigated surface MPs across 43 stations in the eastern Indian Ocean (EIO) during the late northeast monsoon period using in situ pumped sampling, μ-FTIR identification, and 22 environmental indicators spanning productivity, particle optical properties, hydrography, surface dynamics, mixed-layer structure, and maritime exposure. MPs were detected at all stations, with abundances ranging from 6.67 to 160.00 particles m-3 and a mean of 29.37 ± 26.72 particles m-3. This pronounced spatial heterogeneity is consistent with the intrinsic patchiness of open-ocean surface waters, where hydrodynamic transport, convergence, dispersion, and vertical redistribution can generate strong local variability in particle abundance. The regional MP assemblage was dominated by polyethylene terephthalate (PET), fibers, light-colored particles, and small MPs, with particles <200 μm accounting for 52.1% of the total. Elevated abundance was not explained by maritime exposure alone, but was associated with lower primary production, weaker particulate backscattering, warmer surface waters, and weaker surface-dynamic forcing. Using environmental variables alone to define surface-water regimes, we found that MP abundance was significantly higher in warm, low-productivity waters with weaker surface dynamics than in cooler, more productive waters with stronger surface dynamics (mean: 34.64 vs 17.18 particles m-3; Kruskal-Wallis H = 8.57, p = 0.0034). Particle composition, including polymer/material type, morphology, color, and size class, remained broadly similar across regimes. These findings suggest that environmental conditions modulate the surface abundance of an existing regional MP pool.

title: Oxidative Enhancement of Polystyrene Bioconversion Associated with Bio-Fenton-Type Processes in a Mesocosm-Scale Plastivore System.
mesh: Polystyrenes; Oxidation-Reduction; Animals; Iron; Tenebrio; Larva
abstract: Sustainable plastic waste management calls for mesocosm-scale biological strategies coupling polymer depolymerization with controlled plastic-carbon transformation, yet routes for optimizing plastivore-mediated bioconversion beyond laboratory scale remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a mesocosm-scale plastivore-based platform using Tenebrio molitor larvae and show that moderate Fe supplementation increased the •OH-associated oxidative activity, accompanied by enhanced polystyrene (PS) depolymerization and PS disappearance. Under a simplified incineration-reference scenario, the estimated PS-derived carbon conversion flux corresponded to a gross avoided direct-emission potential of up to approximately 0.31 t CO2 per ton of larvae per month, without representing net life-cycle greenhouse gas mitigation. Molecular analyses showed greater oxidative functionalization, oligomer formation, and chain scission than under regular bioconversion. Quantitative •OH assays and fluorescence imaging further showed stronger intestinal •OH-associated levels, faster signal development, and earlier stabilization in the enhanced bioconversion system. Together, the evidence supports Fe-mediated enhancement of intestinal oxidative processes consistent with bio-Fenton-type reactions and identifies redox modulation as a promising and scalable strategy for plastic depolymerization and bioconversion.

title: Divergent Shifts in Sediment Dissolved Organic Matter Stability and Microbial Carbon Metabolic Potential Induced by Biodegradable and Conventional Microplastics.
mesh: Microplastics; Geologic Sediments; Dissolved Organic Matter; Carbon; Biodegradation, Environmental; Polyesters
abstract: Biodegradable polymers are promoted as alternatives to conventional plastics, but their effects on sediment dissolved organic matter (DOM) and microbial communities remain unclear. Here, we estimated impacts of two nonbiodegradable (low-density polyethylene (LDPE) and poly(ethylene terephthalate) (PET)) and two biodegradable (polylactide (PLA) and poly(butylene succinate) (PBS)) polymers on DOM composition and microbial functional profiles using Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS) and metagenomic sequencing. The tested nonbiodegradable polymers shifted DOM toward recalcitrance. In contrast, biodegradable polymers exhibited divergent trajectories: PLA shifted from labile at day 30 to recalcitrant by day 60, whereas PBS showed the opposite trend toward instability. Microbial communities shifted from high-abundance Deltaproteobacteria (∼12%) at day 30 to Alphaproteobacteria (∼16%) and Actinomycetia (∼15%) at day 60. Glycolysis genes were less abundant under LDPE and PET, while fatty acid β-oxidation genes were enriched under LDPE, PET, and PLA. Spearman correlation and Mantel tests revealed that MP-driven DOM changes were associated with microbial community restructuring and bacterial diversity. This study highlights that biodegradable polymers cannot be assumed to have negligible sediment ecological impacts simply because of their degradable classification.

title: Spirocyclic Reconfiguration of the Piperazine Linker Improves Quinoline-Based FAPI PET Tracer Performance.
mesh: Positron-Emission Tomography; Quinolines; Humans; Animals; Piperazines; Fibroblast Activation Protein Alpha; Spiro Compounds; Radiopharmaceuticals; Membrane Proteins; Gelatinases; Serine Endopeptidases; Cell Line, Tumor; Piperazine; Mice; Molecular Dynamics Simulation; Endopeptidases
abstract: Improving the tumor uptake and retention without compromising background clearance remains challenging for fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) radiotracers. Current approaches usually introduce pharmacokinetic modules or reshape molecular scaffolds, increasing structural complexity and synthetic burden. Spirocyclic rigidification offers a distinct strategy by combining conformational constraint and well-defined three-dimensional geometry, yet has not been leveraged for designing FAPI radiopharmaceuticals. Herein, we synthesized FAPI-04 analogues by replacing the piperazine linker with spirocyclic diamines. All analogues were successfully 68Ga-labeled and retained FAP-specific recognition, hydrophilicity and serum stability, but differed in pharmacokinetics and imaging profiles. [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-S1 exhibited higher tumor uptake, longer tumor residence, and improved tumor-to-background contrast than [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 in both HT-1080-FAP and U-87 MG models. Molecular dynamics simulations revealed enhanced local protein-ligand interactions without significant changes in overall complex stability. These findings support spirocyclic replacement of piperazine linker as a feasible strategy for local three-dimensional reconfiguration of quinoline-based FAPI PET tracers.

title: A Biphenyl-Containing Dimeric Sulfonamide PET Tracer for High-Contrast Imaging of Carbonic Anhydrase IX in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma.
mesh: Carbonic Anhydrase IX; Humans; Carcinoma, Renal Cell; Animals; Sulfonamides; Mice; Kidney Neoplasms; Positron-Emission Tomography; Cell Line, Tumor; Radiopharmaceuticals; Tissue Distribution; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Dimerization; Gallium Radioisotopes; Antigens, Neoplasm
abstract: Carbonic Anhydrase IX (CAIX) is an attractive biomarker for clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), but small-molecule CAIX radiotracers are often limited by insufficient tumor retention and suboptimal tumor-to-kidney contrast. Herein, we report the rational design of biphenyl-containing bivalent sulfonamide tracers and evaluation of both 68Ga and Al18F-labeled analogues. Guided by a multivalency strategy, [68Ga]Ga-CAIX-D1 and [68Ga]Ga-CAIX-N1 were developed and compared with the monomeric reference tracer [68Ga]Ga-14. In OS-RC-2 xenografts, both dimers showed higher tumor uptake, improved tumor retention, and tumor-to-kidney ratios greater than 1. The lead scaffold was further adapted to generate [18F]AlF-CAIX-N1, which displayed high tumor uptake, excellent tumor-to-muscle contrast, CAIX-specific uptake, and lower liver uptake than its 68Ga-labeled counterpart. First-in-human positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging further supported its translational feasibility. Collectively, [18F]AlF-CAIX-N1 is a promising tracer for ccRCC imaging and highlights the value of integrating bivalency with radiolabel engineering.

title: [18F]FPyQCP: A Robust FAP-Targeted PET Tracer Integrating Covalent C-18F Labeling and Radiometal Chelation for Enhanced In Vivo Performance.
mesh: Positron-Emission Tomography; Animals; Fluorine Radioisotopes; Fibroblast Activation Protein Alpha; Humans; Radiopharmaceuticals; Mice; Endopeptidases; Serine Endopeptidases; Gelatinases; Membrane Proteins; Chelating Agents; Pyrrolidines; Cell Line, Tumor; Tissue Distribution; Mice, Nude
abstract: Fibroblast activation protein (FAP) is a validated PET imaging target for the tumor microenvironment. Currently, most 18F-labeled FAP PET agents use Al-F chemistry, with Al18F-FAPI-74 leading clinically, whereas C-18F tracers perform less effectively. Here, we developed (4-quinolinoyl)glycyl-2-cyanopyrrolidine (QCP)-based inhibitors incorporating a 6-fluoronicotinamide prosthetic group for stable C-18F labeling. Chelator incorporation improved hydrophilicity and enabled structurally matched radiometal- and 18F-labeled analogs from a common scaffold. The compounds exhibited high FAP inhibitory capacity (Ki = 9.9-56.7 pM) and favorable physicochemical properties (Log P7.4 = -3.1 ± 0.1). The lead tracer, [18F]FPyQCP, was prepared by a one-pot, two-step radiosynthesis in 50-80% yields, with >99% radiochemical purity and molar activity of 74-200 GBq/μmol. In U87 xenografts, [18F]FPyQCP achieved high tumor uptake (23.3 ± 2.1 %ID/g) and favorable tumor-to-blood ratios (12.0 ± 0.3) at 2 h. This modular labeling strategy establishes a versatile platform for next-generation FAP PET tracers and beyond.

title: Albumin-Binding Modification Improves Tumor Retention of Hydrophilic αvβ6-Targeting Radiotheranostic Tracers.
mesh: Animals; Humans; Hydrophobic and Hydrophilic Interactions; Radiopharmaceuticals; Integrins; Mice; Antigens, Neoplasm; Albumins; Cell Line, Tumor; Positron Emission Tomography Computed Tomography; Molecular Docking Simulation; Female; Pancreatic Neoplasms; Carcinoma, Pancreatic Ductal; Mice, Nude; Male
abstract: Integrin αvβ6 is an attractive theranostic target for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Existing αvβ6-targeting tracers are limited by relatively low tumor uptake and rapid tumor washout, compromising theranostic efficacy. In this study, a series of αvβ6-targeting ligands with different hydrophilic linkers and/or albumin-binding moiety were designed and evaluated with molecular docking and MD simulations. Among them, NOTA-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L was selected for further theranostic evaluation due to its favorable targeting capability, enhanced tumor uptake and favorable pharmacokinetic properties. NOTA-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L was labeled with 18F, 68Ga, and 177Lu, and showed favorable in vitro properties, including high hydrophilicity, αvβ6 affinity, and albumin binding. In PET/CT imaging, [18F]AlF/[68Ga]Ga-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L exhibited enhanced tumor uptake and prolonged retention while maintaining favorable pharmacokinetics, showing favorable diagnostic efficiency. In therapeutic studies, [177Lu]Lu-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L effectively inhibited tumor growth with no apparent toxicity. These results demonstrated [18F]AlF/[68Ga]Ga-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L and [177Lu]Lu-Asp2-IPB-αvβ6L as promising radiotheranostic pairs for PDAC.

title: Active surveillance versus standard surgery after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy for oesophageal cancer: long-term results of a cluster-randomised controlled trial (SANO).
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Surgery As Needed for Oesophageal cancer (SANO)-trial demonstrated that active surveillance is non-inferior to standard surgery in terms of two-year overall survival in patients with a complete clinical response after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). Active surveillance resulted in improved quality of life. Here, we report five-year outcomes. METHODS: From 2017 to 2021, a multicentre stepped-wedge cluster-randomised non-inferiority trial was conducted. Patients with locally advanced oesophageal cancer who achieved complete clinical response (defined as no tumour detected on endoscopic biopsies, -ultrasound, or PET-CT) underwent active surveillance or standard surgery. Cox regression was used to compare five-year overall and disease-free survival, and the cumulative incidence of distant metastases was estimated using competing risk analysis. RESULTS: A total of 309 patients were included, 198 underwent active surveillance and 111 underwent standard surgery. Median follow-up was 76 months (IQR 67-86). Five-year overall survival was not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery (50%, 95%CI 43-57 vs. 54%, 95%CI 46-64; HR 1.17, 95%CI 0.77-1.77) with similar results across histologic subtypes. Disease-free survival was not statistically significantly different (HR 1.39, 95% CI 0.94-2.06). The cumulative incidence of distant metastases at five years was significantly higher in the active surveillance group compared to the standard surgery group (46%, 95%CI 39-53 vs. 29%, 95%CI 21-37; P<.01). Overall, 85 of 198 patients (43%) avoided oesophagectomy, including those with sustained complete clinical response at last follow-up or distant metastases detected within six months after nCRT. CONCLUSIONS: Overall survival at five years is not statistically significantly different between active surveillance and standard surgery in patients with oesophageal cancer and a complete clinical response after nCRT, despite a higher incidence of distant metastases in the active surveillance group. These findings support active surveillance as a feasible treatment strategy in selected patients.

title: PET-Guided Dose Escalation for Stage III Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
journal: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys (2026)
abstract: PURPOSE: Uniform radiation dose escalation has not improved outcomes in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and locoregional failure remains common despite multimodal therapy. We evaluated whether fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET)-guided dose escalation to metabolically active tumor subvolumes reduces locoregional failure compared with standard chemoradiation. METHODS AND MATERIALS: PET-BOOST was a multi-institutional, open-label, phase 2 randomized trial conducted at 7 Canadian centers (January 2017-May 2022). Eligible patients had inoperable, FDG-avid stage IIIA/IIIB NSCLC and an achievable boost dose of at least 65 Gy. Patients were randomized 1:1 to standard chemoradiation with 60 Gy in 30 fractions or metabolically adaptive radiotherapy with an integrated boost to FDG-avid subvolumes to a maximum of 85 Gy in 30 fractions. Concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy was planned, and consolidation durvalumab was permitted after 2018. The primary endpoint was 2-year locoregional failure; secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicity, and quality of life (QOL). RESULTS: Seventy-eight patients were randomized: 40 to standard radiotherapy and 38 to dose escalation, with a median follow-up of 5.0 years. Median age was 64.4 years; 53% were male, 62% had stage IIIA disease, and 76% received consolidation durvalumab. Median prescription boost dose was 75 Gy. Two-year locoregional failure was 27.5% with standard radiotherapy versus 18.4% with dose escalation (P=.13). Two-year OS (72.5% vs. 73.7%; P=.91) and PFS (52.5% vs. 57.9%; P=.74) did not differ between arms. Grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicities occurred in 25% versus 37% of patients (P=.26), with one grade 5 pulmonary hemorrhage in the dose-escalation arm. QOL did not differ between arms. CONCLUSIONS: Metabolically adaptive PET-guided radiotherapy dose escalation was feasible in the context of consolidation immunotherapy and resulted in a numerically lower rate of locoregional failure, but did not significantly improve locoregional control or survival. The lower-than-anticipated event rate may have limited statistical power, and larger studies would be required to determine whether selective dose escalation provides a clinically meaningful improvement in locoregional control.

title: Effect of data-driven gating on the quantification of prostate cancer metastases in 68Ga-PSMA- and ¹⁸F-DCFPyL-PSMA PET/CT.
abstract: BACKGROUND: PSMA PET/CT using 18F‑DCFPyL and 68Ga‑labelled tracers is central to prostate cancer staging, but 68Ga‑PSMA may show reduced sensitivity and quantitative accuracy, partly due to respiratory motion and lower spatial resolution. Device-based motion‑correction methods have limitations. Data‑driven gating (DDG) offers a hardware‑free alternative, though its impact on PSMA PET, especially 68Ga‑PSMA has not been systematically evaluated. To evaluate the quantitative and qualitative performance of the DDG motion-correction method in 68Ga-PSMA and 18F-DCFPyL-PSMA PET/CT, focusing on metastatic lymph node, lung, and bone lesions, and to assess its robustness across tracers. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with biopsy‑proven prostate cancer who underwent 68Ga‑PSMA or 18F‑DCFPyL PSMA PET/CT for primary staging or biochemical recurrence and had metastatic disease. Motion correction was applied using the OncoFreeze AI™ data‑driven gating (OFAI‑DDG) method. Metastatic lesions were segmented semi‑automatically, and SUV metrics, image noise, and contrast‑to‑noise ratio were quantified by anatomical site in both OFAI-DDG and static images. Qualitative image quality was independently scored by two experienced readers. Statistical analyses included non‑parametric tests, Bland-Altman agreement, regression analyses, tracer comparison, and inter‑reader reliability assessment. RESULTS: After exclusions, 23 68Ga‑PSMA and 40 18F‑PSMA patients were analyzed, yielding 133 and 192 metastatic lesions, respectively. OFAI‑DDG reconstruction significantly increased SUVmean and SUVmax compared with static imaging for both tracers across bone, lymph node, and lung lesions (p < 0.0001), with the largest gains in lung lesions. CNR improved for most lesion types, and image noise was significantly reduced. Qualitative analysis showed better image quality, sharpness, and noise with OFAI‑DDG, with high inter‑reader agreement. OFAI‑DDG performance was robust across tracers and largely independent of lesion location. CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that OFAI‑DDG significantly improves PSMA PET/CT image quality and quantitative accuracy compared with standard static imaging. The improvements were observed for both 68Ga‑PSMA and 18F‑PSMA tracers, indicating tracer‑independent robustness. The OFAI‑DDG simplified the workflow and reduced time used for patient set-up,

title: Three-dimensional multimodal fractal dynamics integrating spatial metabolism, cytoarchitecture, and perfusion for preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in colorectal liver metastases.
mesh: Humans; Colorectal Neoplasms; Liver Neoplasms; Fractals; Female; Male; Middle Aged; Microvessels; Neoplasm Invasiveness; Aged; Imaging, Three-Dimensional; Preoperative Care; Perfusion; Multimodal Imaging; Preoperative Period; Prognosis
abstract: BACKGROUND: Accurately predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) preoperatively remains a core challenge for precision surgical decision-making in patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM). This study developed and validated a three-dimensional multimodal fractal dynamic model (FRAC-3D) that integrates spatial metabolism, cytoarchitecture, and blood perfusion, aiming to non-invasively identify MVI status preoperatively and evaluate patient prognosis. METHODS: Utilizing a retrospective nested cohort design, stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (sIPTW) was applied to the derivation cohort (n = 100) for baseline debiasing. A core cohort of 145 patients with complete PET/CT, CE-MRI, and DWI imaging was ultimately included. Spatial metabolic fractal dimension (FD_PET), architectural fractal dimension (FD_ADC), and perfusion fractal acceleration (Afd_MRI) were extracted to construct the FRAC-3D model. The model's discrimination, calibration, and clinical benefit were validated in an independent temporal validation cohort (n = 45). RESULTS: Multivariable analysis confirmed that FD_ADC is the strongest independent predictor of MVI (OR = 3.85, 95% CI: 2.45-6.04, P < 0.001). The FRAC-3D model achieved an AUC of 0.938 and a negative predictive value of 96.2% in the validation cohort. Compared with the dual-modal model, FRAC-3D significantly improved risk restratification (continuous NRI = 0.425, P < 0.001). A "highly chaotic" imaging phenotype, identified based on fractal feature clustering, demonstrated an MVI incidence as high as 96.7% and a median recurrence-free survival (RFS) of only 5.2 months. CONCLUSION: Through the cross-validation of multidimensional biophysical features, the FRAC-3D model enables high-precision preoperative prediction of MVI status. This study advances the perioperative assessment of CRLM from traditional 'static anatomical metrics' into a novel dimension of 'microenvironmental dynamic evolution', providing a robust, physics-driven tool for individualized surgical margin planning and the precise stratification of targeted neoadjuvant therapy.

title: 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography with Computed Tomography in Pediatric Non-oncological Conditions: A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: This article examines the expanding role of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) positron emission tomography with computed tomography (PET/CT) in pediatric non-oncological conditions, moving beyond its established oncologic use. It outlines radiation dosimetry principles unique to children-emphasizing the As Low as Reasonably Achievable principle, reduced tracer activity, and low-dose CT protocols-given their heightened radiosensitivity. In pediatric neurology, FDG PET/CT aids evaluation of drug-refractory epilepsy (temporal and extratemporal foci) and neuronal migration/proliferation anomalies like focal cortical dysplasia (FCD), polymicrogyria, and hemimegalencephaly.

title: Tumor volume may be a better indicator than diameter for occult lymph node metastasis in patients with clinical stage-1 lung cancer.
abstract: Occult lymph node metastasis (OLM) remains a major clinical challenge in patients with lung cancer despite comprehensive preoperative staging efforts. Although several predictors of OLM, including tumor diameter, metabolic activity, molecular characteristics, and radiomics, have been extensively investigated, the predictive role of tumor volume remains poorly defined. This study aimed to evaluate whether tumor volume, quantified semi-automatically using artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted Synapse 3D software, could predict OLM in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer. Patients who underwent surgical resection for clinically staged cT1b-cN0M0 lung cancer between 2018 and 2024 were included. Tumor volume was quantified using Synapse 3D software. Associations between tumor volume and OLM were assessed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses. Because tumor diameter and tumor volume may introduce multicollinearity in multivariable models, separate receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated, and the corresponding areas under the curve (AUCs) were compared using the DeLong test. A total of 248 patients were included, of whom 59 (23.8%) were female. The mean age was 65.4 years. OLM were identified in 10.8%, 4.8%, and 2.0% of patients at the N1, N2a, and N2b nodal stations, respectively. Multivariable logistic regression identified younger age (p = 0.004), greater tumor volume (p = 0.01), and histopathological subtypes other than adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma as independent predictors of OLM. Tumor diameter, extent of resection, surgical approach, and PET-CT metabolic activity were not significantly associated with OLM. ROC analysis demonstrated that tumor volume had significantly greater discriminatory ability for predicting OLM than tumor diameter (AUC: 69% vs. 58%; DeLong test, p = 0.004). AI-assisted tumor volumetry is an independent predictor of occult lymph node metastasis in patients with clinically early-stage lung cancer.

title: A Case of Advanced Basal Cell Carcinoma of the Head and Neck: Diagnostic Challenges and Sequential Systemic Therapy.
abstract: Advanced cutaneous malignancies with basaloid morphology can present diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when pathological interpretations differ and disease progresses during systemic treatment. We describe the clinical course of a 53-year-old woman with an extensive, unresectable cutaneous tumor involving the posterior neck and occipital region, accompanied by bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy and additional clinically suspected cutaneous deposits. The initial diagnosis was trichoblastic carcinoma, whereas expert pathological review favored basal cell carcinoma. The extent of disease precluded surgery and definitive radiotherapy. First-line vismodegib was initiated, and palliative radiotherapy delivering 30 Gy in 10 fractions to the occipital lesions and bilateral cervical lymph nodes was completed one year later. Clinical progression was documented three months after completion of radiotherapy; one month after this, MRI demonstrated extensive infiltration involving the left parotid gland and adjacent pharyngeal spaces. Second-line cisplatin and 5-fluorouracil were subsequently administered. Follow-up MRI six months after the earlier MRI demonstrated substantial tumor volume reduction. PET/CT three months later showed a heterogeneous response compared with a year earlier, including regression at several previously involved sites and newly apparent metabolically active right axillary lymph nodes. A subsequent biopsy was reported as basaloid carcinoma. The patient later experienced clinical deterioration, received one cycle of cemiplimab, and died before further treatment or response assessment. This case illustrates the importance of pathological clarification, longitudinal imaging, and careful interpretation of treatment response during sequential systemic therapy for advanced basal cell carcinoma.

title: Whole-body MRI for the evaluation of metastatic lobular breast cancer; current uses and future directions.
abstract: Invasive lobular cancer (ILC) metastases are harder to detect radiologically than invasive breast cancer of no specific type due to a unique tumor biology. Metastatic ILC (mILC) spread is also unusual and challenging, favoring sites such as the peritoneum. The sclerotic bone metastases commonly seen with mILC are non-measurable on CT by currently accepted response criteria (RECIST 1.1.) and are frequently fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET-CT non-avid. UK/European guidelines recommend CT +/- bone scan or PET-CT for staging and assessment of treatment response in breast cancer however there is increasing evidence that Whole-body MRI (WBMRI) with its anatomical and functional capabilities (offered by diffusion-weighted imaging) can overcome conventional imaging challenges for breast cancer, especially for ILC subtypes. WBMRI is more accurate at identifying additional sites of disease in mILC and the earlier detection of progressive disease resulting in treatment changes. WBMRI advancements are creating fast, well-tolerated studies, and the use of novel artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques may increasingly help with acquisition and reporting speed. There are WBMRI consensus guidelines for several tumor types, but no published guidelines yet exist for breast. This review article presents the current evidence to support the use of WBMRI in the management of mILC illustrated by cases from clinical practice and discusses the challenges of widespread adoption and potential future applications.

title: Lithium Amide: A Catalyst for Depolymerization.
abstract: The widespread use of plastic materials leads to significant contamination of ecosystems, posing risks to both wildlife and human health. There is an urgent need for efficient, economical, and environmentally friendly catalysts to depolymerize plastic waste into value-added compounds. In this study, we utilized the easily accessible catalyst [Li{N(SiMe3}2]2.2(THF) and pinacolborane (HBpin) as a hydride donor to convert various types of plastic waste, biodegradable/non-biodegradable polyesters, and polycarbonates into respective borylated value-added alcohols under mild conditions without any pre-treatment, up to 99% yield. The borylated 1,4-benzenediol obtained from polyethylene terephthalate (PET) depolymerization is characterized by single-crystal x-ray diffraction studies, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), and routine spectroscopic techniques. Additionally, the catalyst has been employed for the depolymerization of mixed/contaminated waste plastics, achieving selective and excellent yields of the borylated alcohols. This catalyst facilitated the gram-scale depolymerization of PET into eco-friendly alcohols, such as 1,4-benzene-di-methanol and ethylene glycol, via the depolymerization of PET waste bottles. Furthermore, mechanistic studies supported by Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations provide insights into the catalytic pathway. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first example of alkali metal-catalyzed depolymerization of esters and carbonates containing waste polymers via a homogeneous method.

title: Augmenting Deep Learning-Based PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation With a Population-Level Spatial Atlas.
abstract: Automated lesion segmentation is increasingly central to PSMA PET/CT interpretation, supporting staging, treatment planning, and response assessment at a scale that outpaces available nuclear-medicine expertise. However, automated PSMA-PET/CT whole-body lesion segmentation models are trained on images alone, with no knowledge of where in the body prostate metastases actually tend to occur. Radiologists use clinical domain knowledge of metastatic spread, but its absence in machine learning models produces false positives in anatomically implausible locations and missed lesions in high-risk sites such as the liver. In this work, we explore whether population-level spatial knowledge of metastatic spread can be used to augment deep learning segmentation predictions, and how such a prior should be fused with a network's output, without additional training. We build a data-driven metastasis atlas from 375 expert-annotated whole-body PSMA PET/CT scans and investigate its fusion with a trained segmentation network under a Bayesian framework, in which prediction probabilities from an nnU-Net-based lesion segmentation model serve as the likelihood and the data-driven atlas as the prior. Because metastases occupy only a small fraction of whole-body voxels, the atlas's peak probability is too low, and standard power-scaled or naive Bayesian pooling references lack the tools to deal with this shortcoming. This causes these standard fusion strategies to fail and, in the naive Bayesian case, to sharply degrade performance. We instead derive a calibrated, background-referenced log-odds fusion, one of many possible approaches to combine a population atlas with a deep learning model's predictions, distinct from classical multi-atlas label fusion in that it fuses a single population prior with a trained network's softmax rather than combining several registered atlases. Furthermore, this approach is neutral outside atlas support by construction, reduces exactly to the baseline network when unweighted, and requires no retraining. This atlas fusion significantly improved mean Dice over the baseline nnU-Net on a disjoint internal test set (+0.011, Holm-adjusted p = 0.021) and on an independent external cohort (+0.0129, Holm-adjusted p = 3.8×10 - 16 ), with lesion sensitivity improving from 0.849 to 0.861 internally and Dice improving over baseline in every stratified anatomic reg

title: From task-specific AI to multimodal foundation models in PET/CT: a readiness framework for clinical translation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence in PET/CT is evolving from narrowly optimized systems toward reusable pretrained representations and multimodal models. PET/CT is a demanding test case because clinically meaningful interpretation must preserve quantitative molecular information while integrating anatomic CT, acquisition metadata, longitudinal examinations, and free-text imaging reports. This focused narrative review synthesizes literature reported from January 2021 through July 2026, spanning PET reconstruction and enhancement, attenuation correction, segmentation, outcome modeling, pretrained representations, vision-language systems, and agentic workflows. We distinguish task-specific models, reusable pretrained representations, promptable models, vision-language systems, generalist foundation-model candidates, and agentic systems according to demonstrated capabilities, while separately considering evaluation benchmarks. Task-specific deep learning has demonstrated promising technical performance in low-count imaging and whole-body tumor analysis, but most evidence remains retrospective and restricted by radiotracer, disease, scanner, institution, or endpoint. Emerging PET-native studies demonstrate label-efficient segmentation, image-text grounding, report generation, and modular tool orchestration; however, they do not yet establish broad cross-tracer generalization or prospective clinical benefit. We therefore propose MOSAIC-PET, an author-developed heuristic six-domain evaluation framework for PET/CT foundation models encompassing Molecular fidelity, Organ and anatomic grounding, Semantic faithfulness, Adaptability, Integration and clinical impact, and Continuous governance. MOSAIC-PET has not undergone Delphi consensus or formal validation and is intended to organize PET-specific evidence requirements rather than function as a validated clinical-readiness tool. The near-term translational priority is the development of modular, auditable systems in which validated quantitative tools and evidence-linked language outputs remain under specialist oversight, with progression from external testing to silent evaluation, assisted-use studies, clinical-impact assessment, and continuous lifecycle monitoring.

title: Cancer of Unknown Primary Presenting as Isolated FDG-Avid Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis: Diagnostic Escalation after a Non-Diagnostic Core Biopsy - A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cancer of unknown primary (CUP) remains a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge, particularly when presenting as isolated cervical lymph node disease. Adequate tissue sampling is crucial, and escalation to excisional biopsy may be necessary when minimally invasive procedures are inconclusive. CASE PRESENTATION: A 62-year-old man with a history of long-term tobacco use presented with a right-sided neck mass. Otolaryngologic examination and fiberoscopy revealed no mucosal abnormalities. Fine-needle aspiration suggested metastatic poorly differentiated carcinoma, while core needle biopsy yielded scant, nondiagnostic material. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated pathological right cervical lymph nodes (level III 29 × 29 mm, level IIa 20 × 15 mm). 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography showed an FDG-avid right cervical nodal package at the level IIB/III border (SUVmax 21.1) and an incidental focal uptake in the left thyroid lobe (SUVmax 4.4), with no other suspicious lesions. Thyroid ultrasound revealed a small, well-demarcated hypoechoic lesion (3.5 × 2.6 × 4.5 mm); repeated ultrasound-guided FNAC was benign (Bethesda II), and calcitonin was within the reference range. The patient underwent excisional lymph node biopsy and comprehensive endoscopic evaluation under general anesthesia (panendoscopy with bilateral tonsillectomy and directed biopsies), without identification of a primary tumor. Histopathology and immunohistochemistry confirmed nodal metastasis of undifferentiated carcinoma, most consistent with carcinoma with sarcomatoid features, confined within the lymph node capsule. Because no primary site was identified after imaging, endoscopic evaluation, thyroid workup, and histopathological assessment of the lymph node, the diagnosis remained CUP. The patient was subsequently referred for radiotherapy. CONCLUSION: In cervical lymph node metastasis from CUP, adequate tissue sampling remains essential for definitive diagnosis. When fine-needle aspiration suggests malignancy but core needle biopsy is nondiagnostic, early excisional biopsy should be considered to enable reliable histopathological and immunohistochemical classification. PET/CT may guide the diagnostic pathway and identify incidental findings requiring verification, but imaging should not delay escalation to representative tissue sampling.

title: Challenges in Managing Synchronous Advanced Prostate and Pancreatic Cancers: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Prostate cancer (PCa) and pancreatic cancer (PC) are distinct malignancies with diverging epidemiological and prognostic profiles. PCa often mimics benign prostatic hyperplasia, while PC remains asymptomatic until advanced stages, complicating early detection. As cancer survivorship and screening improve, the incidence of synchronous multiple primary malignancies (MPMs) is rising, with emerging data suggesting a potential biological link between PCa and PC. Managing such cases requires a delicate balance of treatment sequencing and toxicity management. Reporting these rare encounters is vital for refining clinical strategies in complex oncologic presentations. CASE PRESENTATION: This report details the clinical course of a 76-year-old male diagnosed synchronously with high-grade ductal PCa and pancreatic adenocarcinoma. Staging via PSMA PET-CT incidentally identified a pancreatic tail mass with an unusually high SUVmax of 5.2. Despite initiating standard androgen deprivation therapy, the aggressive ductal variant exhibited a "PSA escape" following treatment interruption. As the pancreatic lesion progressed metastatically, the patient's refusal of conventional chemotherapy and a lack of genomic profiling prompted a salvage, "last-resort" combination of pembrolizumab and olaparib. While this strategy achieved temporary biochemical stabilization and slowed tumor growth, the patient eventually succumbed to metabolic dysregulation and multi-organ failure. CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of MPM management, specifically rare PSMA-avidity in primary pancreatic tumors which can mimic metastatic spread. While empirical immunotherapy and PARP inhibitor combinations may offer temporary clinical benefit in resource-limited settings, they cannot substitute for biomarker-guided precision medicine. Success depends on strict therapeutic adherence and early multidisciplinary coordination.
